AUTHOR: Scoulding
TITLE: Evaluating automated benthic fish detection under variable conditions
DATA: Own net-attached Acoustic and Optical System (AOS) stereo stills, 5 deployments (OP12, OP16, OP19, OP24, OP32), July 2019 survey
V_EV: Evaluation (3) Altitude: 'altitude above the seabed affects the levels of illumination... Images were binned at 1 m resolution between the seafloor and 10 m for testing'
D2: Train: starboard images of OP12/16/19 randomly split 80/20 train/val; test: port images of same deployments (in-domain) and of unseen deployments OP24, OP32
D_EV: Datasets: 'Port-side images from OP24 and OP32 were used purely for testing purposes and were not seen at all during the training routines.'
R_EV: Discussion: 'we did not investigate distribution shifts associated with different cameras... as all AOS operations used the same instrument' (all deployments from one July 2019 survey)
C_EV: no statement found (only IoU thresholds 0.3/0.5 for AP; no score threshold value reported)
E_EV: Fig. 4: 'Estimated count of orange roughy from the detector trained on OPall... Data are binned by ground truth count'
ARCH: SSD with ResNet-50 base (GluonCV); DCP preprocessing
METR: AP at IoU 0.3 and 0.5, stratified by fish density, substrate, altitude
NOTE: Mixed test design: in-domain tests use port-side stereo counterparts of the training starboard frames (near-duplicates; authors note 'trained on the same fish but observed from a slightly different angle' -> D4=Y), plus held-out deployments OP24/OP32 (different time/location, same survey). D1 coded at deployment level (사이트/서식지); verifier may prefer lower value. Authors call OP24/32 'out of domain' but per P2 same campaign/camera -> R1=N. V6=Y treats altitude (camera-to-subject range/illumination) strata as quantitative; turbidity itself only mentioned qualitatively; images >10 m altitude excluded for poor light. Pretraining on PASCAL VOC (no matching PRE option) -> PRE=NR. NIMG = 464 stereo pairs x2 + 308 port test images (approx.).
